document_title: NASA National Transonic Facility virtual tour
claim: NTF is a nitrogen/air closed-circuit cryogenic aerodynamic wind tunnel; current tour lists Mach 0.2–1.2 and -250–130 F. Temperature bounds below are conservatively rounded inward to 117–327 K.
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: NASA Common Research Model: Experimental Approach
claim: The documented CRM aerodynamic campaign varied tunnel temperature between 117 and 302 K to reach Reynolds numbers 5, 19.8 and 30 million. This is a source-specific aircraft model test, not a generic cryostat experiment.
quote: the tunnel temperature was varied between 302 K and 117 K
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: NASA Small Multi-Purpose Research Facility
claim: SMiRF has conducted liquid-hydrogen liquid-acquisition-device tests and supports tank chilldown/transfer. Reported minimum -424 F is about 19.817 K; 20 K is a conservatively rounded cold-reach requirement. Source gives 20–80 psi tank pressure but this catalog does not infer a specimen pressure rating from it.
quote: Successful LADs tests have been conducted using liquid hydrogen
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: Hartwig et al., Screen Channel Liquid Acquisition Device Outflow Tests in Liquid Hydrogen
claim: The reported SMiRF experiment used fixed liquid saturation temperatures 20.3, 21.4, 22.9 and 24.2 K. The selected catalog fixture represents only the demonstrated 20.3 K point, not a continuous controllable interval. Section 5.4 identifies the actual SMiRF tank, LAD channels, heaters, outflow controls and thermometry; this was inverted 1-g vertical outflow, not microgravity.
location: Sections 5.4 and 6.1 / Table 3, apparatus and fixed fluid temperatures
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: NASA Creek Road Cryogenics Complex
claim: The 20–90 K calorimeter uses separate warm/cold boundary temperatures and a vacuum vessel. SMiRF thermal shroud temperature is a background boundary, not the liquid-hydrogen sample temperature. Calorimeter vacuum capability is 1e-7 Torr or better.
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: Chato et al., Design and Operation of a Calorimeter for Advanced Multilayer Insulation Testing
claim: NASA's guarded calorimeter was designed for insulation heat-leak tests with nominal 20 K inner and 90 K outer boundaries and a calibrated rod measuring conducted heat flow. These are two simultaneous boundaries, not a uniform 20–90 K sample range.
quote: Design and Operation of a Calorimeter for Advanced Multilayer Insulation Testing
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: Bowens et al., The Michigan Infrared Test Thermal ELT N-band (MITTEN) Cryostat
claim: MITTEN characterizes 8–13 um mid-IR detectors; interior below 40 K, optical bench 16 K, internal source and Offner relay. The paper says filter/aperture mechanisms will be added, so they are not labeled installed. Bench temperature is not asserted to be the detector setpoint.
quote: optical bench maintains a temperature of 16 K
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: NASA Marshall Optics and X-Ray and Cryogenic Facility
claim: XRCF evaluates large optical mirrors/structures down to 20 K; this is a cryogenic optical metrology facility, not an arbitrary microscope cryostat.
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: UAH, Subscale Beryllium Mirror Demonstrator Testing Support, Final Report 521134-FR
claim: The September 2000 SBMD-3 optical test at XRCF measured a 0.532 m beryllium mirror in vacuum near 38 K; Table 4 reports mean temperature 37.87 K. This is an actual mirror measurement point, distinct from the generic facility's cold-reach figure. The procedure requires thermal drift below 2 K/hour and no gradients above 3 K; those bounds are not a universal facility guarantee.
location: Pages 2–4 procedure; page 9 / Table 4, actual cold optical test
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: NASA Marshall Optical Systems Capabilities
claim: NASA describes XRCF's two interferometers measuring structural distortions in cryogenic mirrors, vacuum typically below 1e-6 Torr. This supports the mirror-interferometry function, not a universal nanometer-accuracy guarantee.
location: X-Ray and Cryogenic Facility optical metrology description
verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

verification: Primary source inspected; bounded catalog transcription, not an independent engineering certification.

document_title: Washington State University HYPER, Cubic Cryo Chamber
